correctness.rationale: Every nonzero rank-one square-zero factor has a dyadic description modulo scaling, giving \(C\) factors. For a fixed rank-one target \(B=u\beta\), decompositions \(B=(u\varphi)(v\beta)\) are characterized exactly by \(\varphi(u)=0\) and \(\varphi(v)=1\). Splitting by \(\beta(v)=0\) versus nonzero gives a complete two-by-two transition \(K\), with eigenvalues \(H(H-1)\) and \(-(q-1)q^{n-2}\). Initial state, spectral decomposition, and constant nonzero-product continuation count \(q^{n-1}(q^{n-1}-1)\) determine all target fibers. The trace-class sizes \(C\) and \((q^n-1)q^{n-1}\) establish the exact total-variation formula and support boundary. Direct exhaustive Python enumeration checks every zero and rank-one target in eight small field-and-dimension cases, including a nonprime field; finite checks corroborate but are not a general proof. The symbolic proof has no unverified characteristic restrictions or computational dependence.

value.rationale: The minimal nonzero nilpotent conjugacy orbit is an intrinsic, classical matrix object whose multiplicative convolution powers measure its factorization geometry; the exact all-length, all-target law is more than a small census or textbook existence corollary. The two-eigenvalue phenomenon determines the exact nonzero survival probability and conditional mixing profile and exposes the dimension-two obstruction to two-factor traceless targets. It supplies a reusable distribution and a sharp support classification for arbitrary finite fields and dimensions, distinct from idempotent products.
